source.title: EXPOSE: Explainable and Domain-Robust Embeddings from Pathology Vision Foundation Models using Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Anja Witte; M. Lennartz; Jan Baumbach; G. Sauter; Stefan Bonn; P. Fuhlert; Marina Zimmermann

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether SAE features can be identified in a pathology vision foundation model and carry interpretable domain/task information, extending the indirect-evidence version to a vision model rather than an LLM. It does not test toy-model superposition or LLM feature geometry.
record.gate_note: The study trains an SAE on H0-mini embeddings and reports feature visualizations, cross-domain activation patterns, and effects of masking selected SAE dimensions. These bear on V4 as evidence of recoverable sparse features in a real model, but not on overlapping directions, polysemanticity from capacity pressure, or feature dimensionality. Related work and the chosen hyperparameters are not results.
record.test_reason: The study uses an SAE as a tool on a pathology vision foundation model (H0-mini) to find and mask domain-specific latents for robust relapse prediction. Its quantitative results (Table 1, Tables 3-4, DoRI) measure its own method's downstream performance. The only evidence on whether the features are real is a handful of hand-picked top-activating images (Fig. 3) with no interpretability metric, and the system is a vision model, not an LLM. It does not test whether real models contain SAE-recoverable features as a claim about superposition. V4's named system is LLMs, so no row bears on it as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct, with three qualifications. Masking improved cross-domain relapse prediction relative to the complete SAE representation. The ID optimum is at k=256 and the OoD optimum at k=3500, and ScanA.thin is not improved. The authors also claim that DoRI increases under domain-weighted masking but not under random masking (until k=1024), and they conclude that domain and relapse information are partially separated in the sparse space.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a ReLU SAE with reconstruction and sparsity losses on pathology vision-model embeddings, followed by linear domain classification and feature masking. It does not reproduce the Toy Models of Superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Masking effects depend on the number of masked features and on whether evaluation is ID or OoD; the authors also report differing effects across unseen domains.

fits_no_version.finding: In a pathology vision foundation model, SAE latents ranked by a linear domain classifier align with scanner-dependent activation shifts. Relapse-associated latents occupy different regions of a UMAP, which the authors read as partial disentanglement. The evidence is selected qualitative examples plus a UMAP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents on vision foundation model embeddings separate acquisition-domain information from task information (disentanglement in SAE space).

fits_no_version.finding: Masking top domain-weighted SAE latents changes mean OoD relapse AUROC5 from 60.87 to 62.16 at k=3500 versus the unmasked SAE. The gain is not uniform across OoD domains.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE-based feature masking improves cross-domain robustness of downstream classifiers (application of SAEs, not superposition).

record.problems: The study evaluates one VFM and one ReLU-based SAE on a single internal prostate cancer dataset. Domain features are identified using one pair of acquisition domains. Feature visualizations are selected examples; the study does not test completeness, stability across SAE runs, canonicality, or the geometry of underlying model features. Performance varies across OoD domains.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. DoRI masking curves in Fig. 4C-D concern embedding robustness rather than a measure named by V4, so they are not cataloged as V4 results.

untested.parts: No toy models, overlap geometry or sparsity transition.
No test of capacity competition or of importance-driven allocation.
No analysis of polysemantic neurons or their causes.
No LLM is studied. There is no quantitative test of feature spread across neurons or of SAE feature recovery or interpretability; the SAE is used only as a tool in a vision model.
No completeness, stability-across-runs or canonicality tests; only a single ReLU SAE is used.

record.verdict_notes: The study is an applied SAE-as-tool paper in computational pathology. No result addresses superposition or LLMs. The reader's V4 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels are removed: the rows are either qualitative cherry-picked visualizations or the study's own method's performance, and the subject is a vision model rather than the LLMs V4 names.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transition, and regular geometry are not tested.
Does not test whether feature competition for limited capacity causes polysemanticity or whether importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
Tests SAE-recoverable features in a pathology vision model, not LLMs; does not measure feature spread across neurons.

Does not establish that SAE features are complete or canonical units, or measure their stability across SAE runs. Selected visual examples and cross-domain consistency do not test these properties comprehensively.
Does not test whether underlying model features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: H0-mini
rows.size_stated: Patch embeddings d_in = 768; SAE has 3840 sparse dimensions
rows.operation_detail: Projected pairwise activation deltas between ScanB and ScanA samples for SAE feature dimensions into a shared UMAP space and compared domain- and relapse-classifier weights.
rows.measure: Qualitative organization of feature activation differences and classifier weights
rows.value: Domain weights strongly correspond to scanner-dependent activation shifts; relapse weights show little spatial overlap with domain-specific features. Authors interpret the information as partly disentangled.
rows.note: UMAP is a qualitative analysis; it does not establish completeness or canonical status of SAE features.
rows.check: A UMAP of activation deltas coloured by classifier weights. It concerns domain/task disentanglement within the SAE space, not whether the model contains sparse features. It is qualitative only.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: H0-mini pathology vision model; selected domain- and relapse-associated SAE features, visualized across ScanA and ScanB
reader_labels.reason: Selected SAE features show coherent and often cross-domain-consistent activation patterns, and their weights align with scanner-dependent activation shifts and relapse-related information (R1-R5). This is evidence for recoverable sparse features in this vision model, not LLMs.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: H0-mini cross-domain relapse prediction after feature masking
reader_labels.reason: Masking selected SAE dimensions has mixed effects: large masking improves aggregate OoD AUROC5, but gives a lower mean ID score than the unmasked SAE and the authors report no improvement for ScanA.thin relative to the base model (R6-R10).
